body_html:
Key facts at a glance

  • The four ways to tour Egypt: shared departure, private tour, big-bus package, DIY independent.
  • Shared departure: one tour on one date, filled with travellers pooled from several licensed agencies; four to eight travellers; confirmed at four (the GoAhead).
  • Private tour: vehicle and guide for your party only; your pace; private pricing.
  • Big-bus package: large coach groups on fixed schedules; per-seat pricing.
  • DIY independent: you arrange transport, tickets and guiding yourself.
  • Cost per person: check the current itinerary and departure page; advertised starting prices and the price for your chosen date can differ.
  • Group size, shared: four to confirm, eight maximum.
  • Price rule, shared: fixed per traveller, with no solo surcharge, however the group fills.
  • Operator: a Ministry-licensed, ETAA-registered Egyptian company, named once it accepts the departure and always before your deposit is due.
  • Payment, shared: reserving is free until confirmation. For day tours, the published terms normally specify a 10% deposit at GoAhead and the balance 48 hours before departure. If confirmation happens on or after the balance-due date, the full price is due at confirmation. Packages have a different schedule; check the payment terms shown for your departure before reserving.
  • Cancellation, shared: For standard day tours, the published terms provide a full refund at least 48 hours before departure. Later cancellation or a no-show retains the 10% deposit, with any balance refunded. Disclosed supplier conditions can apply. Check the terms for your departure, including the provisions for unavoidable events; packages have different cancellation bands.
  • Browse: all itineraries and forming and confirmed departures.

Every Egypt itinerary hits the same fork: private guide, group tour, or going it alone. Most of the advice online picks a side instead of comparing them honestly. This guide puts the four ways to tour Egypt side by side, showing how to compare the cost of a Giza day for one, two and four travellers, and the trade-offs in flexibility, company and hassle that the price tags hide. It is written by the people behind Sawa Tours (sawa.tours), the Egypt shared-departure platform. We have worked in Egyptian tourism since 1993, first as a guide and then running an agency, and we have guided private and group days for three decades.

Should I do a private tour or group tour in Egypt?

It depends on three things: how many of you there are, what the tour means to your trip, and how much hassle you are willing to carry. But the honest answer starts with a third option most comparisons skip.

A private tour buys the vehicle, the guide and the pace for your party alone: maximum control at the highest price, and the per-person price falls as your group grows. A big-bus group package is the budget classic: a coach, a schedule and a crowd of strangers. And between them sits the shared departure: a small group of four to eight travellers pooled from several licensed agencies onto one date, with your own Egyptologist guide, a fixed per-person price and no solo surcharge, and nothing charged until the date is confirmed. For solo travellers and couples, that middle option is usually the one that makes the comparison easy.

The four ways to tour Egypt, side by side

Compare the same itinerary, headcount and inclusions. A guided shared day includes services that a ticket-and-taxi DIY budget does not.

Shared departure

  • Group size: 4 to 8, capped
  • Flexibility: Fixed dates, set itinerary
  • Company: A real group of 4 to 8
  • Logistics: Handled
  • Who it suits: Solo travellers, couples, small groups of friends

Private tour

  • Group size: Your party only
  • Flexibility: Total: pace, start times, changes
  • Company: Only your people
  • Logistics: Handled
  • Who it suits: Families, special occasions, full control

Big-bus package

  • Group size: Coach-sized, varies
  • Flexibility: Fixed schedule, fixed route
  • Company: Crowds of strangers
  • Logistics: Handled
  • Who it suits: Ultra-budget travellers happy on a coach

DIY independent

  • Group size: Just you
  • Flexibility: Total, and entirely your problem
  • Company: Alone unless you make friends
  • Logistics: All of it yours: tickets, taxis, heat, haggling
  • Who it suits: Confident, flexible, city-based travellers

How to compare the cost of a Giza day for 1, 2 and 4 travellers

Use the current Giza Uncovered departure price as your shared-tour benchmark. Its listed inclusions cover a guide, transport and the Giza Plateau entrance ticket; optional pyramid interiors and camel rides are extra. Obtain a private quote for the same inclusions, and budget DIY transport and tickets separately.

  • One traveller: compare one shared seat with a private vehicle-and-guide quote and a solo DIY transport-and-ticket budget.
  • Two travellers: compare two shared seats with a private quote for two; divide shared DIY transport costs between you.
  • Four travellers: compare four shared seats with a private quote for four. Check all entrance tickets, guiding and transport are included on both sides.

Three pricing patterns matter when comparing quotes.

  • Shared pricing is per person. Compare one seat, two seats or four seats at the price shown for your chosen departure. The shared model does not make a solo traveller pay for an entire private vehicle.
  • Private pricing can fall per person as your party grows. Ask for separate quotes for one, two and four travellers; there is no universal headcount at which private matches shared.
  • DIY is cheapest per head only if you can do without a guide. The tickets and taxis are real costs either way, but the guiding, the part that turns stones into stories, is the piece you give up.

Flexibility, company and hassle: where each way wins

Flexibility: private wins, DIY is free but earns it

A private tour bends to you: start times, pace, extra stops, skipping what bores you. DIY is even freer on paper, but every change is yours to arrange in a language you may not speak, in heat that punishes bad planning. A shared departure is the least flexible: fixed dates, a set itinerary, and a group of up to eight to keep together. If your dates are rigid and your must-sees are unusual, that rigidity is a real cost, so price it honestly.

Company: shared is the only mode built for it

A shared departure hands a solo traveller a real group: four to eight people, one Egyptologist guide, and a day that is easier for being shared. Private tours are for your people only, wonderful with friends and quiet alone. DIY is solo by default; some travellers love that, others find the temples lonelier than the photos suggest. Big-bus packages put you in a crowd rather than a group: company of a sort, but not the kind you can talk to.

Hassle: DIY carries all of it, the others carry none

On a DIY day you are the operations manager: tickets, taxis, opening hours, the sun, the haggling and the small print. On complex days that burden is the real price. Abu Simbel is a long drive or a short flight from Aswan with an early start, and a Minya day from Cairo is a long round trip. Those are the days confident independent travellers still take tours for. Shared and private days hand all of it to the licensed operator; that is a large part of what the price buys, alongside the guiding itself.

How to choose in five questions

Answer these in order and the right mode usually picks itself.

  • How many of you are there? Solo or a couple: a shared departure carries the guide without a solo surcharge. Four or more: get a private quote and compare it with the shared price for the same itinerary. A party of four can meet the standard four-traveller minimum by reserving four seats; check the date’s availability and confirmation status.
  • Are your dates fixed or flexible? If your dates are fixed, check which shared departures fit them. Flexible dates give you more departures to choose from.
  • What is the budget per person? Below the shared-tour price, DIY or big-bus; above it, private buys control.
  • Do you want to manage logistics in Egypt? Be honest. If not, cross DIY off for the complex days and keep it for the simple ones.
  • Is this day a highlight or a filler? Highlights justify tours and guides; fillers can be DIY.

One more pattern worth naming: most good Egypt trips end up mixing all three. Shared days for the great sites, a DIY morning in the city you are based in, one private splurge on the day that matters most. The modes are not rivals; they are tools.

Common mistakes when choosing

  • Comparing a private per-person price against a shared total (or the reverse). Same itinerary, same headcount, then compare.
  • Assuming "group tour" means a coach. A shared departure of four to eight with your own Egyptologist guide is a different product from a big-bus package, and the difference is the whole point.
  • DIY-ing the complex-logistics days. The long, early, multi-stage days are where a tour earns its price; the city museums are the ones you can do alone.
  • Booking a private tour as a solo traveller and absorbing the whole-vehicle price, when a shared departure delivers a guide and a group without a solo surcharge.
  • Ignoring the confirmation and cancellation terms. A group date that can be cancelled for low numbers after you have paid is a different risk from one where nothing is charged until it is confirmed. Read the deposit, balance and refund terms for any mode before you book.
  • Treating the cheapest quote as the best value. On a guided day, the guide is the product; a licence, an Egyptologist and a small group are what you are actually shopping for.

How to mix all three on one trip

The pattern that works, from watching itineraries succeed over three decades: shared departures for the highlight days, DIY for the flexible city mornings, and one private splurge on the day that matters most to you. On Sawa, a standard shared date confirms at four travellers (the GoAhead), groups are capped at eight, and nothing is charged before confirmation. For day tours, the published terms normally specify a 10% deposit at GoAhead and the balance 48 hours before departure. If confirmation happens on or after the balance-due date, the full price is due at confirmation. Packages have a different schedule; check the payment terms shown for your departure before reserving.

The short version

Private buys control, DIY buys independence and the lowest per-head cost if you are confident and can do without a guide, and shared departures buy a real small group with your own guide at a flat per-person price with no solo surcharge. Compare like for like, ask for a private quote once you are four or more, and mix the modes across your trip: shared for the highlights, DIY for the easy days, private for the one that matters most. tldr: There is no single best way to tour Egypt. The right choice depends on how many of you there are, your budget and how much hassle you want to carry. Private tours buy flexibility at the highest price. DIY is cheapest but you carry all the logistics. Shared small-group departures sit between them: a real group of four to eight, your own Egyptologist guide, a fixed per-person price, and nothing charged until the date is confirmed. Most good Egypt trips end up mixing all three.

faq.q: Is a private guide in Egypt worth the extra cost?
faq.a: For a solo traveller, a shared departure offers a licensed Egyptologist guide without paying for a whole private vehicle. For four or more travellers, obtain a private quote and compare the inclusions and per-person cost. Private guiding can justify the extra cost when control of pace and schedule matters most.

faq.q: Is a shared tour in Egypt safe for solo travellers?
faq.a: A shared departure puts you in a licensed operator's vehicle with a small, confirmed group and an Egyptologist guide, with a named, accountable operator on the departure page. Sawa's WhatsApp (+20 109 284 7613) is answered 24/7 during trips. The group format is a large part of why solo travellers are among the people shared departures suit best.

faq.q: How much more does a private tour cost than a group tour?
faq.a: For one or two travellers, a private day is usually the most expensive option by a clear margin, because the vehicle and guide are priced for your party alone. As the group grows, the private per-person price falls while the shared price stays flat. Get both quotes for the same itinerary and the same headcount before deciding; that is the only comparison that means anything.

faq.q: Do most travellers use just one tour style for a whole trip?
faq.a: No. The trips that work best usually mix the styles: shared departures for the great sites, independent mornings in the cities, and a private day where it counts. The styles are tools, not tribes, and Sawa's itineraries are built to slot into a mixed trip rather than replace it.

faq.q: What happens if I book a shared departure and it doesn't confirm?
faq.a: Nothing is charged before confirmation. A standard shared departure confirms at four travellers (the GoAhead). Check the confirmation deadline shown on your departure. If it never confirms, nothing was charged; browse other dates, including ones that are already confirmed.

faq.q: What are the payment and cancellation terms on a shared departure?
faq.a: Reserving is free until confirmation. For day tours, the published terms normally specify a 10% deposit at GoAhead and the balance 48 hours before departure. If confirmation happens on or after the balance-due date, the full price is due at confirmation. Packages have a different schedule; check the payment terms shown for your departure before reserving. For standard day tours, the published terms provide a full refund at least 48 hours before departure. Later cancellation or a no-show retains the 10% deposit, with any balance refunded. Disclosed supplier conditions can apply. Check the terms for your departure, including the provisions for unavoidable events; packages have different cancellation bands.

faq.q: What if someone in my group doesn't pay?
faq.a: Payment deadlines and any cancellation consequences follow the booking terms. Sawa's GoAhead promise is that a confirmed departure is not cancelled for low numbers if someone drops out. Contact Sawa about your party's payment arrangements before the deadline.

faq.q: Which Egypt sites are easy DIY and which need a tour?
faq.a: City-based sites with simple logistics (the Giza plateau itself, central museums, a dinner cruise) are workable independently for confident travellers. The days that need a tour are the ones where logistics are the difficulty: Abu Simbel, long out-of-town days like Minya, and any site where timing, tickets and transport stack up in the heat.
